questions.question: A number x is mistakenly divided by 10 instead of being multiplied by 10. The percentage error in the result is
questions.solution:
**Concept Used:**

The formula to calculate percentage error, P%, is,

Rightarrow P\%=|(Actual value-Expected value)/(Expected value)| ×100 \%

**Explanation:-**

Given number is x.

Number when it is divided by 10 = (x / 10)

Number, when it is multiplied by 10 = 10x

So, the percentage error 

⇒ P\% = dfrac{(x)/(10)-10x}{10x}×100\ ⇒ P\% = dfrac{x-100x}{100x}×100\ ⇒ P\% = -99\%

Thus, the percentage error in the result is of 99%.

Hence, the correct option is 1.

questions.question: The ratio of the speed of a motorboat to that of the current of water is 31 ∶ 6. The motorboat starts from a point and covers a certain distance along the current in 4 h 10 min. Find the time taken by the motorboat to come back to its initial point.
questions.solution:
**Given**

Total time = 4 hr 10 min.

The ratio of the speed of a motorboat to that of the current of water is 31 ∶ 6.

**Formula used**

Speed = Distance/Time

**Detailed solution:-**

Let the common factor of speeds of a motorboat to that of the current of water be x.

Then, the speed of the motorboat = 31x km/h, 

The speed of the current = 6x km/h.

Motorboat goes along with the current in 4 h 10 m = 4 h +10/ 60 h = 25/6 h 

Speed of downstream = 31x + 6x = 37x km/h

Speed of upstream = 31x – 6x = 25x km/h

Now, the distance covered by the downstream

⇒ speed of downstream × Time taken = 37x × (25 /6) km

Similarly, the distance covered upstream is also 37x × (25 /6)km

 

Time is taken by upstream = Distance covered by upstream/ Speed of upstream

⇒ [37x × (25 /6) ]/25x

⇒ 37/ 6 = 6h + 1/ 6 = 6h 10 min

**∴ The time the motorboat requires to return is equal to 6 hours 10 minutes. **

Let p(x) = x4 + x2 +1,

q(x) = x<span style=" line-height: 0; position: relative; vertical-align: baseline; top: -0.5em;font-size:10
questions.solution:
**Given:**

p(x) = x4 + x2 +1 and q(x) = x4 – 2x3 + 3x2 – 2x + 1. 

If GCD of p(x) and q(x) is x2 - x + 1

Concept:

HCF: Product of the smallest power of each common prime factor in the numbers.

LCM: Product of the greatest power of each prime factor, involved in the numbers

**Formula used:**

a⁴ + a2 +1 = (a2 – a + 1)(a2 + a + 1)

(a + b + c)² = a² + b² + c² + 2ab + 2bc + 2ac

**Calculation:**

We have,

p(x) = x4 + x2 +1

Using the above formula

⇒** p(x) = (x² – x + 1)(x² + x + 1)** ------(1)

⇒ q(x) = x4 – 2x3 + 3x2 – 2x + 1 -----(2)

Also, we have, (x2 - x + 1)

By using the above formula

⇒ (x2 - x + 1)² = x⁴ + x² + 1 + 2(-x)³ + (-2x) + (2x²)

⇒ (x2 - x + 1)2 = x⁴ + 3x² – 2x³ – 2x + 1

Using equation (2)

**⇒ q(x) = (x2 - x + 1)2**

Now we have two polynomial p(x) & q(x)

By using the concept of LCM discussed above

LCM = (x2 + x + 1)(x2 - x + 1)2

**∴ The required LCM is (x2 + x + 1)(x2 - x + 1)²**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] **__Shortcut Trick__**Put x = 2

p(x) = 21 & q(x) = 9 and 

GCD = 22 - 2 + 1 = 3

LCM × HCF = Product of two numbers

21 × 9 = 3 × LCM

LCM = 63

From option (1), at x = 2, we get 63.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **__Important Points__**The greatest common divisor (GCD) of two or more numbers is the

greatest common factor number that divides them, exactly.

It is also called the highest common factor (HCF).

questions.question: A train crosses a man walking at 5 m/sec in the same direction as that of the train in (25)/(2) sec and the same train crosses a man walking at 5 m/sec in the opposite direction as that of the train in (25)/(3) sec. Find the length of the train. (in m)
questions.solution:
**Given:**

A train crosses a man walking at 5 m/sec in the same direction to that of the train in (25)/(2) sec.

The same train crosses a man walking at 5 m/sec in the opposite direction to that of the train in (25)/(3) sec.

**Formula used:**

(1) The length of the train = (s - a) × t

Where, 

s, is the speed of the train

t, is the time taken by the train to pass the walking man.

a, is the speed of man walking is the same direction to that of the train

(2) The length of the train = (s + a) × t

Where, 

s, is the speed of the train

t, is the time taken by the train to pass the walking man.

a, is the speed of man walking toward the train

**Calculation:**

Let S be the speed of the train. (in m/sec)

In the first case:

The relative speed = (S - 5) m/sec

The time is taken by the train to cross the walking man = (25)/(2) sec

The length of the train = (S - 5) × (25)/(2) m

In the second case:

The relative speed = (S + 5) m/sec

The time is taken by the train to cross the walking man = (25)/(3) sec

The length of the train = (S + 5) × (25)/(3) m

On equating the length of train, we get,

⇒ (S - 5) × (25)/(2) = (S + 5) × (25)/(3) 

⇒ (S - 5) × (1)/(2) = (S + 5) × (1)/(3) 

⇒ 3(S - 5) = 2(S + 5)

⇒ 3S - 15 = 2S + 10

⇒ S = 25 m/sec

Therefore, 

The length of the train = (25 + 5) × (25)/(3) m = 250 m

**∴ The required answer is 250 m.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__** **Formula used:-**

Distance = time × Relative speed

**Calculation:-**

*Let speed of train be v m/s,*

When man walking in same direction at 5 m/s-

Distance = 25/2 × (v - 5) = Train length 

∴ Train length = 25/2 × (v - 5) ...(i)

When man walking in opposite direction at 5 m/s-

∴ Train length = 25/3 × (v + 5) ...(ii)

From eqⁿ (i) = eqⁿ (ii)

⇒ 25/2 × (v - 5) = 25/3 × (v + 5)

⇒ 3v - 15 = 2v + 10

⇒ Train speed(v) = 25 m/s

From eqⁿ (i)

Train length = 25/2 × (25 -5) = 250 m

∴ **Required train length is 250 m.**

questions.question: Mohan and Sohan can finish a field work in 50 days, Sohan and Ram in 30 days, while Ram and Mohan in 60 days to finish the same work. How long will they take to finish the work together?
questions.solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

Total Work = LCM(50, 30, 60) = 300 units.

Efficiencies: (Mohan + Sohan) = 6, (Sohan + Ram) = 10, (Ram + Mohan) = 5.

Combined efficiency of 2 × (Mohan + Sohan + Ram) = 6 + 10 + 5 = 21.

Efficiency of (Mohan + Sohan + Ram) = 21 ÷ 2 = 10.5 units/day.

Time = 300 ÷ 10.5 = 200 ÷ 7 = 28 ⁴/₇ days.

**∴ The correct answer is 28 ⁴/₇ days.**

**__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Time taken by Mohan and Sohan = 50 days

Time taken by Sohan and Ram = 30 days

Time taken by Ram and Mohan = 60 days

**Formula Used:**

Total Work = LCM of all given days

Efficiency = Total Work ÷ Number of Days

Time taken = Total Work ÷ Total Efficiency

 **Efficiency**

**Calculations:**

⇒ Sum of given efficiencies = 6 + 10 + 5 = 21 units/day

⇒ 2 × (Efficiency of Mohan + Sohan + Ram) = 21

⇒ Efficiency of (Mohan + Sohan + Ram) = 21 ÷ 2 = 10.5 units/day

⇒ Time taken by all three = Total Work ÷ Total Efficiency

⇒ Time taken = 300 ÷ 10.5

⇒ Time taken = 3000 ÷ 105 = 200 ÷ 7 days

⇒ Time taken = 28 ⁴/₇ days

**∴ The correct answer is 28 ⁴/₇ days.**

**__Additional Information__**

Work and Wages

Wages are directly proportional to the amount of work done. If people work for the same duration, their wages are distributed in the ratio of their individual efficiencies.

Pipes and Cisterns

The concept is identical to Time & Work. Inlet pipes have positive efficiency (filling) while outlet pipes are considered to have negative efficiency (emptying).

Alternate Day Working

When workers work on alternate days, calculate the work completed in one full cycle (e.g., 2 days for 2 workers) and multiply to reach just below the total work before finishing the rest sequentially.

questions.question: The average of the numbers 253, 245, 325, 120 and 115+2K is 212. Find the average of the numbers 353, 354, 225, 220 and 110+3K.
questions.solution:
**Given:**

Numbers: 253, 245, 325, 120, 115 + 2K

Average of these numbers = 212

Numbers for second part: 353, 354, 225, 220, 110 + 3K

**Formula Used:**

Average = (Sum of Numbers) / (Number of Items)

**Calculation:**

Find the value of K using the given average for the first set of numbers.

Sum of first set of numbers = 253 + 245 + 325 + 120 + (115 + 2K)

⇒ Sum = 1058 + 2K

Average = Sum / 5

⇒ 212 = (1058 + 2K) / 5

⇒ 1058 + 2K = 212 × 5

⇒ 1058 + 2K = 1060

⇒ 2K = 1060 - 1058

⇒ 2K = 2

⇒ K = 1

Use K = 1 to find the average for the second set of numbers.

Numbers: 353, 354, 225, 220, (110 + 3K)

⇒ Numbers = 353, 354, 225, 220, (110 + 3 × 1)

⇒ Numbers = 353, 354, 225, 220, 113

Sum = 353 + 354 + 225 + 220 + 113

⇒ Sum = 1265

Average = Sum / 5

⇒ Average = 1265 / 5

⇒ Average = 253

**The average of the numbers is 253.**

questions.question: Average of the marks of 132 students of a college is 40. If the average of the marks of the passed students is 42 and the average of the marks of the failed students is 20, then what will be the respective ratio of the total marks of passed students and the total marks of failed students?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] **__Shortcut Trick__**

The ratio of the number of passed students to failed students

= (40 - 20) : (42 - 40) = 10 : 1

Suppose number of passed students = 10x

⇒ The number of failed students = x

Total marks of passed students = 42 × 10x = 420x

Total marks of failed students = 20 × x = 20x

∴ Required ratio = 420x : 20x = 21 : 1

**Detailed Solution:**

Average of marks of 132 students = Sum of marks of 132 students/132

⇒ 40 = Sum of marks of 132 students/132

⇒ Sum of marks of 132 students = 5280

Let number of passed student be x

Number of failed student = 132 – x

Now,

Average of marks of passed student = sum of marks of passed students/x

⇒ 42 = sum of marks of passed students /x

⇒ sum of marks of passed students = 42x

Now,

Average of marks of failed student = sum of marks of failed students/(132 – x)

⇒ 20 = sum of marks of failed students /(132 – x)

⇒ sum of marks of failed students = 20(132 – x) = 2640 – 20x

Now,

Total sum = 42x + 2640 – 20x

⇒ 5280 = 22x + 2640

⇒ 22x = 2640

⇒ x = 120

Total marks of passed student = 42x = 42 × 120 = 5040

⇒ Total marks of failed student = 2640 – 20x = 2640 – 20(120) = 240

∴ Required ratio = 5040 ∶ 240 = 21 ∶ 1

A sum of Rs. 8,400 amounts to Rs. 11,046 at 8.75% p.a. simple interest in a certain time. What will be the simple interest (in Rs.) on a sum of Rs. 10,800 at the same rate for the same time?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Simple Interest 1 (SI₁) = 11,046 − 8,400 = ₹2,646

Since Rate (R) and Time (T) are constant, Simple Interest is directly proportional to Principal (P).

Ratio of Principals (P₁ : P₂) = 8,400 : 10,800 = 7 : 9

Required Interest (SI₂) = (SI₁ ÷ 7) × 9 = (2,646 ÷ 7) × 9

SI₂ = 378 × 9 = ₹3,402

**∴ The correct answer is ₹3,402.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Case 1: P₁ = ₹8,400, A₁ = ₹11,046, R = 8.75%

Case 2: P₂ = ₹10,800, R = 8.75%, T is same as Case 1

**Formula Used:**

SI = (P × R × T) ÷ 100 | Amount (A) = P + SI

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/fd451624316375341976e37561baaeec5cf3c698bb3fd739c00d4a910b8aff59.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ SI₁ = A₁ − P₁ = 11,046 − 8,400 = 2,646

⇒ Since R and T are same, SI₁ ÷ P₁ = SI₂ ÷ P₂

⇒ 2,646 ÷ 8,400 = SI₂ ÷ 10,800

⇒ SI₂ = (2,646 × 10,800) ÷ 8,400

⇒ SI₂ = (2,646 × 108) ÷ 84

⇒ SI₂ = (2,646 × 9) ÷ 7

⇒ SI₂ = 378 × 9

⇒ SI₂ = 3,402

**∴ The correct answer is ₹3,402.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Direct Proportionality in Simple Interest

When rate (R) and time (T) are constant, the simple interest (SI) varies directly with the principal (P). If P increases by a factor, SI increases by the same factor.

Effective Rate of Interest

The effective simple interest over a period T is simply (R × T)%. For example, 8.75% for 4 years is an effective 35% of the principal.

Relationship between SI and Amount

Amount = P(1 + RT/100). The ratio of Amount to Principal is (100 + RT) : 100.

questions.question: The ratio of the number of boys to the number of girls in a class is 2 ∶ 5. If 10 boys leave the class and 20 new girls join the class, then the new ratio of boys and girls in the class becomes 4 ∶ 25. What is the number of boys in the class now?
questions.solution:

The ratio of the number of boys to the number of girls in a class is 2 ∶ 5. 

If 10 boys leave the class and 20 new girls join the class, then the new ratio of boys and girls in the class becomes 4 ∶ 25

**Formula used:**

ratio of x and y = (x)/(y)

**Calculation:**

Let the number of boys in the class before be 2x. Then, the number of girls in the class at that time is 5x

When 10 boys leave the class and 20 new girls join the class, then the new ratio is,

⇒ (2x-10)/(5x+20)=(4)/(25)

Solving for x,

⇒ 50x - 250 = 20x + 80

⇒ 30x = 330

⇒ x = 11

Number of boys in class earlier = 2 × 11 = 22

**∴ The number of boys in the class now is 22 - 10 = 12.**

Marked Price = 50% above the Cost Price

Net Discount = 30 + 25 – [(30 × 25)/100]

⇒ 47.5%

47.5% of 150x = 47.5/100 × 150x

⇒ 71.25x

SP = 150x – 71.25x

⇒ 78.75x

 = 100x – 78.75x = Rs.21.25x

According to the given question,

21.25x = 850

⇒ x = 40

⇒ 78.75x = 40 × 78.75 = 3150

**∴ He sold it at Rs. 3150**

questions.question: One quality of rice at Rs. 45 per kg is mixed with another quality at a certain rate in the ratio of 3 ∶ 2. If the mixture so formed is worth Rs. 50 per kg, what is the rate per kg of the second quality of rice?

Average rate of product = Total price of product/quantity of product

Rice of second type of rice = 2x

Rate of second type of rice = Rs.A/kg

According to the question:

⇒ 135x + 2Ax = 50 × 5x

⇒ 135 + 2A = 250

⇒ 2A = 250 - 135 = 115

⇒ A = 115/2 = Rs.57.5/kg

**∴ The correct answer is Rs.57.5/kg**
